deep.reconstruction:
Context: draft material for Riemann's 1859 Göttingen memoir 'Ueber die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 8, 1860) and its self-announcement (Selbstanzeige) in the Göttinger Nachrichten. The previous page holds the main text: Riemann invariants, characteristic speeds, and the shock-jump relation. The page has no new mathematics. It contains (A) draft prose, (B) a unit conversion of Joule's mechanical equivalent of heat done with 7-place logarithms, (C) Regnault's density data, and (D) data on the speed of sound.

(A) Two drafts.
- First draft sentence: through the complete solution of the problem he believes he has brought to a clear decision two things. One is the question debated among English mathematicians, presumably Challis versus Stokes/Airy (1848-51) and Earnshaw (1858-60) on plane waves of finite amplitude. The other is a dispute carried on in some 'Ges. d. W.' / Academy, place illegible (my conjecture: the Vienna Academy, Petzval versus Doppler, 1852).
- Second draft, a cover letter: 'Ew. Hochwohlgeboren erlaube ich mir gehorsamst beiliegend eine Anzeige der am 21. d. eingereichten Abhandlung zu übersenden und um deren Aufnahme in die Nachrichten zu bitten.' It is addressed to the Secretary of the Königliche Gesellschaft der Wissenschaften and forwards the self-announcement of the memoir.

(B) Joule's equivalent, 772 English foot-pounds per lb of water per 1°F, converted to metre-kilogram per kg per 1°C. With 1 ft = 0.3048 m and 1°F = 5/9 °C:
- J = 772 · 0.3048 · 9/5.
- Logs: log 0.3048 = 9.4840071-10; log 772 = 2.8876173; log 1.8 = 0.2552725.
- Sum = 2.6268969, so J = 423.542 m·kgf per kgf per °C.
- Result written: 772 engl. F. Kilogr./1°F = 423.542 m Kilogr./1°C.

Two abandoned columns:
- Column 1: log 772·0.3048 = 2.3716244; + log 2.25 (0.3521825, struck) = 2.7238069; + log 0.45359 (pound→kg, 9.6566707) = 2.3804776, i.e. about 240.2.
- Column 3: adds both the pound factor and 1.8, giving 2.2835676, i.e. about 192.1.
- These are false starts. The pound/kg factor cancels in a per-unit-mass quantity.

(C) Regnault (Pogg. Ann. 74, p. 202; Relation des expériences, Paris 1847) gives these weights in Paris for one litre:
- air at 0° and 0.76 m: 1.293187 g;
- water at maximum density: 1000.000 g;
- mercury at 0°: 13595.93 g.
- Hence ρ_Hg/ρ_air = 13595.93/1.293187 = 10513.5 (checked).
- He also cites Regnault on the specific heats of gases (P.A. 89 p. 335; C.R. 36 p. 676), which gives c_p(air) = 0.2375.

(D) Speed of sound:
- Bravais & Martins (P.A. 66 p. 351; Ann. chim. phys. (3) 13 p. 5): 332.37 m/s.
- Moll & van Beek, 27-28 June, 14 reciprocal shots: mean 332.25 m/s, spread 0.66 m.
- Reduction factors in Regnault's manner: sqrt(1+0.00366 t) for temperature, and sqrt(1-0.38x) for humidity, with x = e/p (vapour pressure over total pressure).

Purpose (my reconstruction, not on the page): this is Mayer's route to the mechanical equivalent through k = c_p/c_v obtained from the speed of sound.
- Newtonian speed: c_N = sqrt(g · 0.76 · 10513.5) ≈ 280 m/s.
- Ratio of specific heats: k = (332.37/280)^2 ≈ 1.41.
- Gas constant of air: R = p0/(ρ0 T0) ≈ 29.27 m/K.
- Then J = R / (c_p(1-1/k)) ≈ 424 m·kg/kg/°C.
- This agrees with Joule's 423.5 computed in (B).
errors: Column 1 multiplies by 2.25 (log 0.3521825, later struck) and then by the pound-to-kg factor. Both are inappropriate for the per-unit-mass equivalent, and the column was abandoned.
Column 3 includes the pound-to-kg factor (9.6566707). It cancels for a per-mass quantity, so 192.1 is meaningless; Riemann correctly kept 423.542 from the second column.
Moll & van Beek's experiments took place 27-28 June 1823 (published Phil. Trans. 1824). The date '1824' is likely the publication year or a slip.

The humidity factor is written sqrt(1-0.38x). Since moist air is lighter, a measured speed must be multiplied by this factor to reduce it to dry air (equivalently, c is proportional to 1/sqrt(1-0.38 e/p)). The note is consistent only if read as a reduction factor.

results.what: Regnault's air/mercury density ratio 10513.5 at 0°C, 760 mm

results.what: Draft claim that the 1859 memoir settles the English controversy (Challis/Stokes/Airy/Earnshaw) and another academy dispute

deep.surprise_reason: These are draft letter text and routine numerical bookkeeping (unit conversion, Regnault data, sound-speed values) belonging to Riemann's well-known 1859/60 shock-wave memoir and its self-announcement. Nothing here is mathematically new.

checkable.asserts: equals about 2.6268969, so the product is about 423.54
Mayer-type mechanical equivalent ≈ 424 m·kgf/kgf/°C, consistent with Joule's 423.5

transcription_corrections: In the first log column the struck line reads 0,3521825 (log 2.25), not 0,2552725.

Line 1: the illegible place is probably the dispute in 'der k. Akad. d. W. zu Wien' (conjecture: Petzval vs Doppler). The bracketed fragments should be read as 'Durch die vollständige Lösung der Aufgabe glaube ich die zwischen den englischen Mathematikern verhandelte Frage ... ferner den Streit ... zu klarer Entscheidung gebracht zu haben'.
'423,542' was written under the first column but is the antilog of the second column (2,6268969).
The final '332m 37' is the Bravais & Martins value, aligned below the Regnault reduction factors.
The humidity factor reads sqrt(1-0,38x) with x presumably e/p.
Folio number '48' is visible at upper right.
